leads.summary: Repeated image directory entries now append duplicate thumbnail-index records
leads.consequence: A cold invocation with the same image directory twice writes the same path/signature/hash twice to index.tsv, despite generating one thumbnail. The value added to thumbnail_index inside thumbnail_for is lost when line 284 runs the function through command substitution; the preloaded map cannot see entries created during this invocation. The picker cache index grows needlessly across repeated overlapping image inputs and makes subsequent cold opens slower. Base's per-image awk scan saw its previous append and wrote only one index row. Fix by preserving index updates in the parent shell or deduplicating inputs/append under a lock.

leads.summary: Disk staging test still cannot detect a broken stop or misplaced dial reset
leads.consequence: A mutant that removes the read-transition assignment at Panel.qml:93 still passes the string assertion because Panel.qml:63 clears the field in runTest. Likewise tracking the stager's PID while removing pkill of its children leaves the string assertion true and the test invokes only a normally completing stage, so pgrep at line 127 finds no writers. Tests can pass while cancellation leaves writers or read retains the write sample. Add a simulated mid-staging TERM test that records and waits on owned stub dd PIDs, and assert the read transition's updateLine behavior rather than a substring anywhere in the QML.

leads.summary: Batch test accepts a popped window that is never resized or centered
leads.consequence: The test stub returns success for any --batch content. Removing the resize dispatch at bin/omarchy-hyprland-window-pop:49 leaves the existing assertions (one batch and float/pin/tag) satisfied, but the real popped window would keep its previous size. Similarly the default center and z-order action are not asserted. Assert all actions and order in the submitted batch; do not rely on the successful stub exit to show those commands ran.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Follow-up on head `d99f6e18`, after the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12248#issuecomment-5835095823) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12248#issuecomment-5835469552). Three of the four earlier findings are resolved. The window-pop fallback finding is unchanged, because that code was not touched. The branch now has a test-file conflict with current `quattro`. One statement in the earlier review was wrong and is corrected below.

| Earlier finding | Status on `d99f6e18` |
|---|---|
| Stopping the panel during staging leaves the staging writers running | Resolved |
| WRITE dial keeps a partial staging sample through the read phase | Resolved |
| Index load runs on every picker open, including rows-cache hits | Resolved |
| Window-pop fallback cannot run with a real `hyprctl` | Still present |
| Optional test note on `disk-speedtest-stage-test.sh` | Partly addressed |

### Resolved: staging writers stop with the panel

**Verified:** `worker_pids+=("$stager")` now follows `stager=$!`, so `cleanup` → `stop_workers` stops the staging subshell's `dd` children. The poll loop's `sleep 1 & wait $!` lets the trap run at once. A stubbed comparison like the earlier one (synthetic `dd` simulating a 6 s pass, fake block stat file, signal sent 0.3 s after all 4 writers started, 3 runs each; `8463da6d`'s exit time is the rest of its 1 s poll sleep, so it differs from the earlier table):

```text
                               quattro          8463da6d          d99f6e18
SIGTERM to script PID          0 of 4 writers   4 of 4 writers    0 of 4 writers
  script exit                  0.015 s          0.716 s           0.007 s
SIGINT to process group        0 of 4 writers   4 of 4 writers    0 of 4 writers
(writers alive when the script exits)
```

**Correction:** The earlier review said "A terminal Ctrl-C still stops them, since it signals the whole process group." That was wrong for `8463da6d`: SIGINT to the process group also left all 4 writers running through their full pass. With job control off, bash starts `( ... ) &` with SIGINT ignored, and GNU `dd` keeps an inherited ignored SIGINT, so only `cleanup` could stop them. On `d99f6e18` both paths stop the writers, so no further change is needed.

**Optional test improvement:** Both new checks in `disk-speedtest-stage-test.sh` are text greps. `grep -Fq 'writeMBps = ""'` already matches the reset in `runTest()` (`Panel.qml:63`, also present on `quattro`), and a copy of this head with only the new `read`-branch reset removed still passes the test. The `worker_pids+=("$stager")` grep catches deletion of that exact line but not the stop behavior. A case that sends SIGTERM to the script during staging and checks stub-recorded `dd` PIDs would cover the fix.

### Resolved: WRITE dial dims during the read phase

**Verified (source reading):** The `read` branch in `Panel.qml` now sets `writeMBps = ""`. The WRITE dial's value becomes 0 while it is not live, so `SpeedTestOverlay.qml` draws it at 0.5 opacity through the read phase and after a read-phase failure. The write phase sets it again, and no `read` line follows, so the final write figure stays.

### Resolved: index load only on cold picker opens

**Verified:** The `index.tsv` load now runs only in the cold branch, after both rows-cache checks. Median wall time, `--cache-only`, 200 synthetic images plus 20,000 other index rows, stubbed thumbnail generator (sandbox timings on one machine; read as relative):

```text
case                     quattro   8463da6d   d99f6e18
rows-cache fast hit      11 ms     174 ms     11 ms
signature hit            146 ms    325 ms     151 ms
cold, thumbnails exist   2.75 s    0.58 s     0.56 s
```

`index.tsv` and the signature files were byte-identical to `quattro` after every step, the rows caches matched apart from each run's own cache directory, the same thumbnail files were created, and the thumbnail generator ran the same number of times.

### Still present: window-pop fallback cannot run with a real `hyprctl`

`bin/omarchy-hyprland-window-pop` and `test/shell.d/window-pop-batch-test.sh` are unchanged since the earlier review. In Hyprland's current `main` (`hyprctl/src/main.cpp`), `batchRequest` still returns `void` and discards the IPC result, so `--batch` exits 0 once past its pre-send checks, as in v0.56.2.

**Impact:** Unchanged from the earlier review. The per-step fallback in `hypr_flush` is unreachable, the third test case asserts an exit status the real client does not produce, and dispatch errors are discarded. As the earlier review found from source reading, no window end state differs from `quattro`.

**Suggested change:** Drop the fallback and that test case, or inspect the batch reply for `error:` lines if errors should be reported (that needs the reply, which `hypr_flush` currently sends to `/dev/null`). Replaying the whole queue after a partly applied batch would toggle pin and float a second time.

### New: conflict with current `quattro` in `menu-images-test.sh`

`quattro` commit `24f12431` (#13403) appended a `--print-rows` test block at the end of `test/shell.d/menu-images-test.sh`, where this PR appends its index check. GitHub reports a merge conflict for this branch. `bin/omarchy-menu-images` merges without conflict.

**Impact:** GitHub marks the branch as conflicting until this is resolved. The conflict is limited to the test file.

**Suggested change:** Rebase or merge `quattro` and keep both test blocks. With both kept, all three PR test files and `quattro`'s new `--print-rows` test pass, and `--print-rows` output matches the rows cache.

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `d99f6e18` against the previously reviewed head `8463da6d`, `quattro` merge-base `9c5482c5` and the current `quattro` tip `3faafba2`, plus Hyprland v0.56.2 and current `main`, Quickshell v0.3.1, GNU coreutils `dd` and bash source. Command-only sandboxed runs executed the PR's tests on head and on a local merge with the current `quattro` tip, test mutants, a SIGTERM/SIGINT-during-staging comparison, and an image-picker equivalence and timing comparison. `dd`, block device statistics, mount and disk tools, `hyprctl` and the thumbnail generator were stubbed. No compositor, desktop panel or real disk was exercised; the panel display and `hyprctl` exit status rest on source reading.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
